first_hunter_context.bar: Autoliv's own collected consensus, updated 2026-10-19, 20 analysts: Q3 2026 sales $2,718m (range 2,638-2,765), adj EBIT $253m, adj EBIT margin 9.3% (9.1-9.6), EPS $2.18 (1.83-2.40); FY2026 adj EBIT margin 10.4% (below the company guide of around 10.5-11%), Q4 adj EBIT margin 13.9%. https://www.autoliv.com/investors/consensus-estimates . Company guide (Q2 release 2026-07-17): Q3 adj operating margin 'around the first half 2026 level' (H1 = 9.3%), FY organic ~0%, adj op margin ~10.5-11%, LVP -2.5%, raw material gross headwind ~$110m. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001034670/000119312526306698/alv-ex99_1.htm . Second estimate source: Benzinga Q3 EPS $2.21 / revenue $2.72bn (snippet only, page 403). Two sources plus a company guide agree on the margin bar, so the bar is sourced.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: MarketBeat short interest, record date 2026-09-30 (published 2026-10-09): 4,931,143 shares short, 6.76% of float, 6.2 days to cover, up 7.29% from 4,595,987 at the prior record; a year earlier (2025-09-30) it was ~2.5% of float and 3.1 days, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/ALV/short-interest/ . Baseline skew_25d -2.83 vol points (25d call IV above put IV: upside paid), put/call OI 1.37 on thin OI (1,719), run-up +4.71% over 5 sessions and +3.13% over 20, spot 9.6% below the 52-week high. Short base is elevated for a large-cap supplier and building, but not crowded in the 18-23% squeeze sense.

evidence.text: The consensus EPS bar ($2.18, Autoliv consensus page 2026-10-19) sits about 5% below what the same consensus adj EBIT ($253m) converts to: Q3 2025 turned $271m adj EBIT into $2.32 adj EPS on ~77m shares, and shares outstanding fell from 73,237,217 (10 July 2026) to 72,006,695 (30 Sept 2026, 1,232,671 retired in Q3), so an in-line $253m EBIT maps to roughly $2.28-2.32 adj EPS; the EPS low of $1.83 suggests some estimates in the average are not on an adjusted basis.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name sells headline quarters: Q2 2026 (adj EPS $2.43, record Q2 sales, guide kept) -3.78; Q3 2025 (record Q3 sales, op income and EPS) -2.62; 5 of the last 7 reactions negative, the two positives both Q1 prints.
evidence.why_not_priced: Wire headlines will compare reported adj EPS to the $2.18 average; a stale or GAAP-mixed estimate in that average makes an in-line EBIT read as a 'beat'. If the market had arbitraged it, the EPS consensus would sit at ~$2.30 alongside the $253m EBIT, which it does not. Partly priced by anyone who models EBIT, which the sell side does, hence small.
evidence.independence: Share count from Autoliv's 30 Sept 2026 share-retirement release (https://www.inderes.se/en/releases/autoliv-retires-repurchased-shares-decreases-number-of-issued-shares-12) and the Q2 10-Q cover (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001034670/000119312526306974/alv-20260630.htm); Q3 2025 EBIT-to-EPS conversion from https://www.autoliv.com/press/financial-report-july-september-2025-2397395 . Consensus drifted down from ~$2.26 (July 22 snapshot) to $2.18, i.e. the bar was lowered: https://www.autoliv.com/es/node/565 (snippet).

evidence.text: S&P Global Mobility puts Q3 2026 global light-vehicle production at -1.6% y/y (cited in Valeo's Q3 sales release, 2026-10-22), better than the ~-3% H2 run-rate implied by Autoliv's FY assumption of -2.5% after H1 (Q1 -3.4%, Q2 -0.3%); but the regional split derived from Valeo's table (North America ~-5%, China ~-6%, Europe ~0%, Asia ex-China ~+4.5%, South America ~+6%) hits the Americas, where Autoliv underperformed LVP by 4.9pp in Q2 (32% of sales), so applying Q2's regional outperformance gives organic roughly -0.5% to 0% and sales near, perhaps ~0.5% below, the $2,718m bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 organic +3.9% trailed LVP +4.6% and the stock fell -2.62; Q1 2026 organic +0.8% vs LVP -3.4% (4.2pp outperformance) bought +6.82; Q2 2026 outperformance ~1.3pp with Americas -4.9pp sold -3.78. Outperformance vs LVP is the line this name trades on at the top line.
evidence.why_not_priced: The S&P quarterly actual reached the public only via Valeo's release the evening before Autoliv reports; consensus sales ($2,718m, updated 10-19) predates it. If priced, auto-supplier estimates would have been revised in the last day; Autoliv's consensus page shows no update after 10-19. Proxy: regional figures are derived (Valeo LFL minus its stated outperformance), not published by S&P.
evidence.independence: Regional Autoliv outperformance pattern and 32/30/19/19 regional mix from Autoliv's own Q2 2026 release and call (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001034670/000119312526306698/alv-ex99_1.htm ; https://www.autoliv.com/sites/autoliv/files/pr/Autoliv_Q2_2026_webcast_transcript.pdf). Shares the Valeo document with the Valeo peer finding below (different line: volume here, guidance there). GM's own NA wholesale +3.6% (finding below) cuts against the derived NA -5%.

evidence.text: Raw-material inflation from the Persian Gulf conflict did not ease in Q3 and Autoliv named helium (an airbag-inflator input) as the main driver: Autoliv's gross headwind estimate rose from ~$90m (Q1 call) to ~$110m (Q2), Nippon Sanso raised helium prices >30% from July 2026, and Hormuz commodity transits were 4 vessels on 15 Sept against ~125/day pre-war; the FY guide of 10.5-11% needs ~14-15% Q4 margin on customer compensations, so a trim toward or below the low end is the main downside on the print, against a consensus already at 10.4%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: guide kept but margin cadence pushed to Q4 and raw-material headwind raised to $110m, stock -3.78. Q4 2025 print (2026 first guide) -4.11. Guidance-cadence news has been sold on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced at the FY level: consensus FY margin 10.4% already sits below the 10.5% low end, so a guide narrowed to 'around 10.5%' is close to neutral. What is not priced is a cut below 10.4% or a larger raw-material number (helium price increases dated July onward land in H2 costs). If the market expected a cut, Q4 consensus margin would sit well below 13.9% and the skew would be put-bid; it is call-bid (-2.83).
evidence.independence: Helium: https://apps.digitimes.com/news/a20260625PD216.html (Nippon Sanso +30% from July 2026, snippet), https://energynewsbeat.co/?p=230143 (Hormuz transits mid-Sept, snippet); resin PPI +10.7% to July 2026 https://www.berlinpackaging.com/content/market-insights/Industry-Update-Q3-2026-English.pdf (snippet, notes PE easing). Q1 $90m figure via https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-4-18-autoliv-inc-stock/ (snippet). Counterweight sized in: Valeo confirmed its FY guide on 10-22 in the same cost environment.

evidence.text: Short interest rose to 6.76% of float / 6.2 days to cover at 30 Sept 2026 (up 7.3% on the prior record and from ~2.5% / 3.1 days a year earlier) while the Q3 EPS consensus was cut from ~$2.26 (July) to $2.18 (Oct 19), so the bar has been lowered and shorts have built for a guide disappointment; a held guide meets a short base that needs ~6 days of volume to cover.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print in the baseline carried this level of short interest; the two up-reactions (Q1 2025 +5.56, Q1 2026 +6.82) both came on prints that cleared a lowered bar after a weak tape.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 25d skew already pays upside (-2.83) and the stock ran +4.7% in five sessions into the print, so part of a cover is likely done or priced; this finding is the residual squeeze mechanism if the guide holds. If fully priced, short interest would have fallen into the print rather than risen at the last record.
evidence.independence: Consensus drift from Autoliv's consensus page snapshots (https://www.autoliv.com/investors/consensus-estimates vs the July 22 snapshot via https://www.autoliv.com/es/node/565, snippet). Baseline skew and run-up are independent market data pointing the same way.

evidence.text: Valeo, reporting Q3 sales on 2026-10-22 in the same input-cost environment, confirmed its FY2026 guidance and said H2 operating margin and FCF will be at least H1 levels, with Q4 sequential growth in line with seasonality; a peer that holds a margin guide the day before is weak evidence that Gulf-driven cost inflation has not broken European supplier guides.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No cited history of ALV trading on a peer's guide; Q2 2026 ALV kept its own guide and fell -3.78.
evidence.why_not_priced: Released the evening before; ALV's spot was sealed at 13:09 ET on 10-22, before or around Valeo's release. Reuters reported Valeo's sales slightly below the €4.93bn consensus, so the read is mixed and small.
evidence.independence: Same Valeo document as the LVP finding (different line). Reuters via https://www.globalbankingandfinance.com/valeo-posts-lower-sales-auto-industry-weakness-persists/ on the sales miss cuts against it.

evidence.text: GM's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-20) shows GM North America wholesales of 870k against 840k a year earlier (+3.6%) and a FY EBIT-adjusted guide narrowed to $14.5-15.5bn with the $15.0bn midpoint unchanged, a firmer North American customer read than the ~-5% NA LVP implied by Valeo's table, relevant to Autoliv's weakest region (Americas, 32% of sales).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Americas organic -3.3% (4.9pp under LVP) in Q2 2026 coincided with a -3.78 reaction; no cited history of ALV moving on GM's print.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public for two sessions, so likely partly in the +4.7% five-day run-up; one customer, not the industry. Small for that reason.
evidence.independence: Cuts against the Valeo-derived NA production figure in the LVP finding; the two are kept separate because one is a single customer's own wholesale number and the other an industry series.

first_hunter_context.bar: Q3 2026 revenue about $294M, from two agreeing estimate sources: Zacks $293.84M (+17.8% y/y; https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/3008486) and Benzinga $294.2M (snippet_only, page 403; https://www.benzinga.com/quote/APPF/earnings-forecasts). FY2026 company guide is $1.117-1.127B revenue and 26.5-28.0% non-GAAP operating margin (Q2 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001433195/000143319526000056/appfq22026exhibit991.htm). The non-GAAP EPS bar is disputed ($1.77 Zacks vs $1.69 Benzinga), so findings that depend on EPS are capped small.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 2,441,935 shares, 7.0% of float, 8.65 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement (FINRA via MarketBeat, published 2026-10-09; https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/APPF/short-interest/). Up from 1.32M in January 2026 and stable at 2.3-2.7M since March. Days to cover rose from 5.2 in mid-August to 8.65 as volume fell. Skew -4.4 vol points (upside paid), put/call OI 0.17, so call-heavy. 20-day run-up +7.5%, 16% below the 52-week high and 53% above the 52-week low.

evidence.text: The FY2026 guide of $1.117-1.127B, with H1 revenue of $543.3M (Q1 $262.2M + Q2 $281.1M), implies H2 revenue of $573.7-583.7M, about +16.4% y/y at the midpoint against +19.7% in H1. Management said 2026 seasonality would be 'broadly consistent with 2025'. Applying 2025's Q2-to-Q3 sequential step (+5.7%, $236.0M to ~$249.4M) to Q2 2026 gives a Q3 of ~$297M (+19% y/y), about 1% above the $294M consensus. Street FY (~$294.2M Q3 + $287.0M Q4 + H1 = ~$1.1245B) sits at the guide midpoint, so a raise of the FY range above $1.127B is the likely outcome.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue +1.4% vs $277M Zacks and FY raised, stock +0.67%. Q1 2026: FY raised, +11.16%. Q3 2025: beat and FY raise (with margin cut), +7.94%. Q4 2025: initial FY26 guide below Street, -8.31%. The guide direction is the line this name trades on.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus at $294M (+17.8%) already sits above the guide-implied ~16% H2 growth, so part of the beat is priced. Benzinga records beats of 0.7-1.6% in each of the last four quarters, so a ~1% beat is the expected outcome. Only the size of the raise is open. If a bigger raise were priced, the run-up and skew would be larger, and the stock is still 16% below its 52-week high.
evidence.independence: Q1 2026 release (Q1 revenue $262.2M, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001433195/000143319526000021/appfq12026exhibit991.htm); Q3 2025 release for the 2025 sequential base (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1433195/000143319525000140/appfq32025exhibit991.htm); seasonality quote from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15278807508870144). All are company documents, so this is one inference resting on the company's own numbers.

evidence.text: Subscription services growth slowed to 14% y/y in Q2 2026 ($59.8M) from 18% in Q1 ($58.2M). The FY outlook 'assumes a more moderate pace of unit expansion among existing customers'. Units were 9.6M (+8%), flat from Q1's 8%. If subscription growth slips further toward ~12% in Q3, the market's core-health metric weakens even on a headline beat carried by value-added services (78% of revenue, +22%).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed this deceleration alongside a raise and the stock moved only +0.67%, which suggests the deceleration offset the raise. No cleaner single-line history is available.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is public, so it is largely priced. What is not known is the Q3 trajectory: consensus is given only at total revenue level, so a further subscription slowdown would not show up as a headline miss. Short interest held near 7% of float all year, which is consistent with part of the market holding this view.
evidence.independence: The company's own words on 'more moderate pace of unit expansion' come from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15278807508870144). This is the same document family as finding 1, but a different line. Shrunk from -0.8 because days to cover is 8.65.

evidence.text: RealPage's 3Q 2026 data: absorption of about 69,800 apartment units in July-September, ahead of Q3 2025 but well below the decade seasonal average for the peak leasing quarter. Occupancy 95.4%, flat on Q2. Effective rents +0.9% y/y and +0.8% q/q. Sun Belt metros are still cutting rents. September payrolls were +29k and the Fed raised rates in September. Lower peak-season move-in volume is a soft input for FolioScreen and move-in services; firmer rents are a small positive for payments volume.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of APPF reacting to an industry leasing series. Value-added services growth (screening, payments, FolioGuard) has driven revenue upside in each of the last quarters.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a multifamily-wide series, and AppFolio's customer base leans to SFR and small multifamily third-party managers, so transmission is weak and not confirmed by the company. The rest of value-added services (payments, FolioGuard attach) grew 22% and outweighs screening volume. Sized small for that reason.
evidence.independence: Proxy only, a single secondary write-up of RealPage's release. No company or counterparty confirmation.

evidence.text: Easy margin comparison: Q3 2025 non-GAAP operating margin was 23.5%, depressed by a $13M incremental bonus accrual (5.5% of revenue). 2026 has run at 27.3% (Q1) and 27.1% (Q2), and the FY guide was raised to 26.5-28.0%. A ~27% Q3 margin means operating profit up roughly 35-40% y/y. The EPS bar is disputed ($1.69 Benzinga vs $1.77 Zacks), so the direction of an EPS 'beat' headline is unclear.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 cut its margin guide on the bonus accrual and still rose 7.94% on revenue and the guide raise, so margin is secondary on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: consensus EPS already shows +30-35% y/y. Capped small because the two EPS estimates disagree by $0.08, and the outcome inside that gap decides the headline.
evidence.independence: Q2 2026 release for the current margin run-rate (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001433195/000143319526000056/appfq22026exhibit991.htm).

evidence.text: Short interest is 7.0% of float (2.44M shares) with 8.65 days to cover at 2026-09-30, up from 1.32M shares and ~3 days in January 2026. Options are call-heavy (put/call OI 0.17, 25-delta skew -4.4 upside paid). On a beat-and-raise, covering of an 8-9 day short base adds a mechanism for an outsized up-move; on a miss, call holders unwind.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 raised its guide with short interest at 2.3-2.5M shares and the stock rose 11.16%. Q2 2026 printed with 2.5-2.7M short and the stock rose 0.67%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Skew and call open interest already show the upside lean, so this mainly widens the move rather than setting its sign. Days to cover rose from 5.2 to 8.65 since mid-August as volume fell, so the short base is harder to exit than at the last two prints.
evidence.independence: The sealed baseline's options block (skew -4.4, put/call OI 0.17) points the same way. It is a different source (Yahoo options) but the same positioning theme.

evidence.text: The CEO sold 2,057 shares at $205 on 2026-08-14 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted around 2025-08-14. Shares were also withheld for tax on 2026-08-10. Routine; no open-market buying or unusual selling cluster found.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: none
evidence.why_not_priced: Nothing to price: a pre-set plan sale. Filed so the judges see that the insider angle was checked.
evidence.independence: Nasdaq write-up of the same sale: https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/appfolio-ceo-william-trigg-sells-2057-shares

first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 11,813,489 shares = 8.71% of float, 3.2 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-30 (published 2026-10-09), up 24.9% from 9,457,002 on 2026-09-15 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/DECK/short-interest/) and roughly double the ~5.8m shares at the 2026-07-15 settlement (curvedtrading via search snippet). evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior DECK print in the baseline carried a short base this size that I could source; the name's reactions are large both ways (-20.5, -19.9, +11.4, -15.2, +19.5, +4.0, -0.2), and the +19.5% on 2026-01-29 came off a depressed, sceptical setup.

evidence.text: Two sell-side channel checks say HOKA US demand softened in the September quarter: UBS (Jay Sole) says its proprietary data show HOKA and UGG trends softer than thought in recent months and HOKA US demand cooled vs Q1, with web-traffic data as a partial offset; BMO (Kelly Crago, Underperform, $70, initiated 2026-09-08) says HOKA US DTC may have turned negative in Q2. Against this, Q1 global HOKA DTC was +17% and management said on 2026-07-23 there was 'not a significant change' in DTC for Q2; HOKA international (double digits) and UGG (~50% of Q2 revenue) are the rest of the company.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: HOKA US deceleration drove the -15.2% on 2025-10-23 (FY guide below consensus) and the -19.9% on 2025-05-22; a HOKA beat with flat guide on 2026-07-23 drew -0.2%.

evidence.text: Revenue from estimate changes on prior-period performance obligations (catch-ups) added 8.1% of revenue in Q1 2026 and 7.7% in Q2 2026, against 4.0% in Q3 2025, 4.4% in Q2 2025 and 1.7% in Q3 2024. About $230-250m a quarter of H1 revenue, at high incremental margin, came from favourable re-estimates. That puts the quality of the 25.9-26.3% gross margin at risk if Q3 catch-ups revert toward the 4% of a year ago, which would take roughly 2-4 points of revenue and some margin off the quarter.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior case of margin disappointing on FIX in the baseline. The last two prints, with gross margin at records (Q1 26.3%, Q2 25.9%), still fell -2.7% and -5.3%, so the market was already discounting margin quality.
evidence.why_not_priced: The figure sits in the revenue-recognition note of the 10-Qs and appears in no release, preview or call highlight read here. Previews quote the gross margin and the backlog, not the share of revenue from re-estimates. If it were priced, Q3 consensus EPS ($12.70-12.85, slightly above Q2's $12.53 on +3-4% revenue) would imply margin compression rather than a flat-to-up margin.
evidence.independence: The Q1 10-Q (8.1% vs 5.8%, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1035983/000110465926047689/fix-20260331x10q.htm) and the Q3 2025 10-Q (4.0% vs 1.7%, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1035983/000110465925101821/fix-20250930x10q.htm) are the same company's documents, not independent confirmation.
